messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the oscillating body and the viscosity coefficient of the surrounding medium. Medium viscosity, which is a property of the fluid or gas, sets the scale of energy dissipation. Dissipation becomes non-negligible when the pendulum moves through a resistive environment. Environment resistance is particularly relevant for a physical pendulum when its damping ratio is appreciable. Appreciable damping must be included when one observes measurable decay of the oscillation amplitude. Amplitude decay over several cycles signals that the viscous friction term cannot be dropped from the equation of motion. Motion of the physical pendulum in such a resistive setting also demands accounting for viscous friction during high-precision experimental measurements. Measurements of the period or logarithmic decrement then require the damping coefficient as an additional parameter. Parameter estimation of the damping coefficient improves the overall accuracy of the physical pendulum model.
